attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: The missing Yang-Mills estimate is a uniform reflection-plane trace theorem for the locked gauge-invariant algebra. It must control contact terms of curvature composites, cusp/edge divergences of Wilson-loop observables, and possible boundary renormalizations as \(T_\delta F\to F\).
steps: Fix a finite positive-time gauge-invariant observable vector \(F=(F_1,\ldots,F_N)\) and coefficients \(c\in\mathbb C^N\). The desired OS inequality is \(Q_S(F,c)\ge0\).
For \(\delta>0\), replace each observable by its collar version \(F_i^\delta=T_\delta F_i\), so reflected and unreflected supports are separated by a gap \(2\delta\).
At the cutoff level, reflection positivity gives \(Q_{a,L}^{\delta}(F,c)=\sum_{i,j}\overline c_i c_j S_{a,L}(\Theta F_i^\delta,F_j^\delta)\ge0\).

Use the RG-to-OS domination assumption for fixed collars to pass to the continuum: \(Q_{a,L}^{\delta}(F,c)\to Q_S^{\delta}(F,c)\). Since \([0,\infty)\) is closed, \(Q_S^{\delta}(F,c)\ge0\). This is the valid closed-cone step.
Invoke the trace modulus \(|Q_S(F,c)-Q_S^{\delta}(F,c)|\le\omega_{F,c}(\delta)\), with \(omega_{F,c}(\delta)\to0\), to identify \(Q_S(F,c)=\lim_{\delta\downarrow0}Q_S^{\delta}(F,c)\).
Conclude \(Q_S(F,c)\ge0\) as a limit of nonnegative real numbers, provided the trace modulus is same-theory and no boundary defect has been inserted or subtracted.
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: The derivation assumes exactly the hard analytic fact: that RG convergence valid away from the reflection plane extends continuously to reflected probes whose supports collide with the plane. Without this, fixed-collar OS positivity may be true while full OS positivity for the intended continuum Yang-Mills Schwinger functions remains unproved.

assumptions: For every cutoff \((a,L)\), the regulated gauge-invariant functional is reflection-positive on the cutoff positive-time algebra.
For each fixed \(\delta>0\), the observables \(T_\delta F_i\) are represented in the cutoff algebra by the same observable-identification maps used to define the continuum theory.
For each fixed \(\delta>0\), RG convergence implies convergence of every finite reflected collar quadratic form.
The continuum functional has a trace modulus \(\omega_{F,c}(\delta)\to0\) controlling the collision of reflected supports with the plane \(t=0\).
The trace modulus is intrinsic to the original gauge-invariant algebra; it is not obtained by adding boundary degrees of freedom or imposing a new reflection-plane renormalization prescription.
definitions: source object: a cutoff net \(S_{a,L}\) of gauge-invariant regulated Schwinger functionals on reflected lattice/continuum observables, with \(Q_{a,L}(F,c)\ge 0\) for all finite positive-time observable vectors \(F\) in the cutoff algebra.

target object: a continuum Schwinger functional \(S\) on a fixed gauge-invariant Euclidean observable algebra \(\mathcal A_+\), satisfying OS reflection positivity \(Q_S(F,c)\ge 0\) for all finite \(F\subset \mathcal A_+\).

controlled interface: RG convergence must dominate the reflected quadratic probes \(Q^{\delta}_{a,L}(F,c)\) for every fixed collar distance \(\delta>0\), and the continuum limit must admit a trace modulus \(Q_S^{\delta}(F,c)\to Q_S(F,c)\) as \(\delta\downarrow0\).

same-theory condition: the collar-shifted observables \(T_\delta F\) converge back to \(F\) in the locked continuum gauge-invariant observable topology, with no \(\delta\)-dependent change of algebra, no boundary counterterm, and no replacement by a different renormalized observable.
\(\Theta\) is Euclidean time reflection with orientation reversal for loop observables and complex conjugation on coefficients.
\(T_\delta\) is a positive-time collar insertion: it translates or mollifies the time support of every factor of \(F\) into \(t\ge\delta\) while preserving gauge invariance.

equations.label: collar quadratic form
equations.valid_when: This formula is valid when \(T_\delta F_i\) has support in \(t\ge\delta\), \(\Theta T_\delta F_i\) has support in \(t\le-\delta\), and both are evaluated in the same gauge-invariant continuum observable algebra.

equations.label: fixed-collar closed-cone passage
equations.valid_when: The RG cutoff-removal topology controls the finite reflected collar probe indexed by \((\delta,F,c)\).

equations.label: boundary trace modulus
equations.valid_when: Valid only after proving that reflection-plane contact terms, cusp divergences of loop observables, and composite-field renormalizations do not create a residual boundary defect.

equations.label: full OS positivity from collars
equations.valid_when: Every fixed-collar form is nonnegative and the trace modulus is same-theory continuous.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: A decisive falsifier is a sequence of gauge-invariant observables approaching the reflection plane for which \(Q_S^{\delta}(F,c)\) has a finite or divergent boundary defect not equal to \(Q_S(F,c)\).
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: This lemma converts the branch from a pure closed-cone observation into a two-stage bridge: fixed-collar positivity follows formally from closedness, while full OS positivity is reduced to a Yang-Mills boundary-value estimate.
candidate_lemmas.statement: Collar-to-boundary OS positivity extension: if the RG continuum limit preserves reflection positivity for every fixed positive-time collar and the continuum Schwinger functional has a same-theory trace modulus as the collar is collapsed onto the reflection plane, then the limiting Schwinger functions are OS-positive on the full gauge-invariant positive-time test algebra. The closed-cone step is valid for fixed collars; the new content is the boundary trace estimate.

assumptions: \(\mathcal D_+\) is dense in the intended physical gauge-invariant test algebra, not merely in an enlarged auxiliary algebra.
The collar maps \(T_\delta\) preserve \(\mathcal D_+\) and are strongly continuous as \(\delta\downarrow0\).
Schwinger distributions obey enough local regularity to make the OS quadratic form closable on \(\mathcal D_+\).
Approximation by \(\mathcal D_+\) commutes with reflection, multiplication of observables, and the cutoff-removal maps.
definitions: Let \(\mathcal D_+\subset\mathcal A_+\) be a reflection-stable positive-time dense core generated by smeared traces of curvature and smoothed loop holonomies with support separated from \(t=0\) before taking the trace limit.
Let \(\|F\|_{\mathrm{obs}}\) denote the cutoff-removal observable topology norm or seminorm family supplied by the RG compactness theorem.
Closability means: if \(F^{(n)}\to0\) in \(\mathcal A_+\) and \(Q_S(F^{(n)}-F^{(m)},1)\to0\), then \(Q_S(F^{(n)},1)\to0\).

equations.label: core approximation of OS forms
equations.valid_when: The OS form is closable and the approximants converge in the same observable topology used to define the continuum Yang-Mills theory.

equations.label: two-limit interchange
equations.valid_when: A uniform trace modulus holds on bounded observable-topology sets, not just pointwise on a chosen approximating sequence.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: A falsifier is a gauge-invariant observable approximable in ordinary distribution topology but not in OS form topology, causing positivity on the smooth core to fail to extend.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: This lemma would make the trace obligation attackable: prove estimates first for smooth, collar-separated representatives, then extend by density and closability.
candidate_lemmas.statement: Dense collar-core reduction: it is enough to prove the collar-to-boundary trace modulus on a dense subalgebra of heat-kernel-smeared local gauge-invariant observables and smooth Wilson-loop cylindrical functions, provided the OS quadratic form is closable with respect to the continuum observable topology.

assumptions: The fixed-collar positivity theorem has already produced \(Q_S^{\delta}(F,c)\ge0\) for every \(\delta>0\).
The limit \(Q_S^{0+}(F,c)=\lim_{\delta\downarrow0}Q_S^{\delta}(F,c)\) exists as a finite quadratic form.
The intended OS form \(Q_S(F,c)\) is independently defined by the original Schwinger distributions.
definitions: Define the boundary defect by \(B(F,c)=\lim_{\delta\downarrow0}Q_S^{\delta}(F,c)-Q_S(F,c)\), whenever the limit exists.
A defect is same-theory trivial only if it is forced to vanish by the original continuum Schwinger distributions and observable identifications.
A defect is theory-changing if removing it requires adding boundary counterterms, altering Wilson-loop renormalization at reflection contact, or changing the positive-time algebra.

equations.label: defect decomposition
equations.valid_when: Both the collar boundary value and the intended OS evaluation exist on the locked gauge-invariant algebra.

equations.label: positivity obstruction
equations.valid_when: The boundary defect is not known to vanish and is not controlled by a positive semidefinite bound compatible with the original theory.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: If an explicit loop or curvature observable yields \(B(F,c)\ne0\), the bridge must either prove \(B=0\) by Yang-Mills estimates or concede that the positivity statement is for a modified boundary theory.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: This gives a diagnostic for whether a proposed positivity proof has silently changed the theory at the reflection plane.
candidate_lemmas.statement: Boundary-defect obstruction criterion: if the collar limit exists but differs from the intended full-plane OS quadratic form by a nonzero bilinear defect \(B(F,c)\), then the closed-cone argument proves positivity for a modified theory unless \(B\) vanishes or is separately shown to be positive-compatible in the original algebra.

control_decision.pivot_test: Pivot if even free/linearized gauge-invariant curvature observables or abelian Wilson loops exhibit a nonzero reflection-plane boundary defect under the proposed collar topology.
control_decision.promotion_test: Promote if a uniform trace modulus is proved on a dense same-theory gauge-invariant core and the RG topology is shown to dominate all fixed-collar reflected quadratic forms.
control_decision.reason: The branch continues to produce sharper obligations. It should not pivot yet because the bridge has become a precise trace-modulus problem with identifiable Yang-Mills estimates and falsifier tests.

The topology must include or dominate seminorms \(S\mapsto Q_S^{\delta}(F,c)\) for fixed \(\delta>0\), together with a uniform trace-modulus mechanism as \(\delta\downarrow0\).
dependency_updates.status: needs reflected-probe domination plus boundary trace estimate

dependency_updates.description: A new explicit dependency was exposed: prove that no cusp, contact, or boundary composite counterterm survives in \(Q_S^{\delta}\to Q_S\).

falsifiers: falsifier: an RG compactness topology that controls ordinary Schwinger distributions but not the mixed reflected seminorms \(S(\Theta T_\delta F_i,T_\delta F_j)\) for fixed \(\delta\).
falsifier: a Wilson-loop family whose reflection-plane cusp renormalization produces a nonzero defect \(B(F,c)\), so the collar boundary value is not the intended OS quadratic form.
falsifier: curvature-composite observables with reflection-plane contact terms requiring a boundary counterterm; this would make the closed-cone argument valid only for a modified theory.
falsifier: the collar map \(T_\delta\) converges in a weak distribution topology but not in the OS quadratic-form topology, preventing \(Q_S^{\delta}(F,c)\to Q_S(F,c)\).
falsifier: the cutoff observable embeddings depend on \(\delta\) or on the side of the reflection plane, meaning the proof has changed the gauge-invariant test algebra across the limit.
branch_outputs.mathematical_learning: Cycle 174 isolates the exact non-tautological bridge. Reflection positivity is not lost in the fixed-collar continuum passage: that part is a valid closed-cone argument once RG convergence controls reflected probes. The unresolved mathematical content is the trace modulus at the reflection plane. This estimate is also the same-theory certificate: if the collar limit requires subtracting a boundary defect, adding a counterterm, or changing Wilson-loop renormalization at the plane, then the proof may preserve positivity but for the wrong theory. The most useful next work is therefore not another abstract topology name, but a model trace estimate for a dense gauge-invariant core and a search for a concrete falsifier among cusp loops or curvature contact terms.
branch_outputs.next_experiment: Test the trace modulus first in a controlled Gaussian/linearized Yang-Mills model for smeared curvature observables: compute \(Q_S^{\delta}(F,c)-Q_S(F,c)\) as \(\delta\downarrow0\), identify the required Sobolev trace regularity, then repeat for a smoothed rectangular Wilson-loop observable approaching the reflection plane to see whether a cusp-defect falsifier appears.
